HOW STATUS IS SET
Designed — a screen exists where the feature is operable, in the states it needs. Partially designed — visible on a screen but not fully specified, or missing a state. Spec card only — written up as a behaviour note with no pixels. Not yet — nothing.
TWO COLUMNS ADDED
REL and MOSCOW are carried from the backlog. They were not in the brief's column list; they are here because deciding which batch comes next is unreadable without them. Say the word and they come out.
UPDATE RULE
This board is regenerated from the same spreadsheet each batch, so a backlog edit propagates. Status is the only field we write by hand.
BATCH J · DOMAINS O, P, Q, S, T · AND THE FINAL SWEEP
EVERY ROW NOW HAS A STATUS
295 designed · 48 partial · 55 spec-card only · 13 not yet. The 13 remaining are the ones we refused with reasons already on this board: F25 and L-domain translation, D06/D07 calls and voice notes, and eight A/B/R items that duplicate mechanisms built elsewhere. Nothing is unaccounted for.
55 SPEC CARDS, NOT 55 FAKE SCREENS
Encryption, pen testing, backup replication, rate limiting, observability, feature flags, deprecation policy and the integration connectors are on J5 as spec cards — each naming what it does, why it has no UI, and where a user would notice if it stopped working. Drawing a key-rotation dashboard would have inflated this board and misled anyone reading it.
THREE THINGS NEEDING A FOUNDER DECISION
N22 CC0 vs CC BY default for external contributions — argued both ways on I7, neither pre-selected. P10 / P20 the contract-research marketplace and an open-source community edition are business decisions before they are screens; the marketplace needs a conflict-of-interest policy that does not exist. L08 generated alt-text is the one held-back AI feature we recommend shipping next, with the same human-review gate as method extraction.
BATCH I · DOMAINS M AND N · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
DESIGNED · 31 of 44
Camille's whole product: console with the policy-override table, SAML/eduGAIN with a live test connection, SCIM including the leaver case, the pilot dashboard, output and integrity dashboards, funder exports, chargeback, confidential mode as a re-skinned tenant, the patent gate, hash-chained audit with SIEM streaming, invention disclosure, vendor and job pages, the six GDPR rights with the statutory clock, privacy centre, consent, ToS versioning, takedown, DSA statement of reasons and appeal, the three-tier moderation queue, the enforcement ladder, impersonation, licence choice, transparency report, hazards and liability.
PARTIAL · 8 · AND WHY
M05 white-label reuses confidential mode's re-skin without its own branding editor. M13 retention is a policy row and a log statement; eDiscovery search is not drawn. M20 procurement appears as export formats, not an integration. N12/N13/N14 paper-mill, export-control and biosecurity screening surface as rows on the integrity dashboard with their routing named, but each needs its own detection-and-review screen. N15 human-subjects fields live on D2's ethics record. N19 breach notification is described in the privacy centre without its incident runbook.
SPEC ONLY · 5 · AND ONE OPEN DECISION
M15 contract-research marketplace and M19 grant discovery are adjacent businesses, not features — each needs its own commercial model before a screen. N18 age verification is not meaningful for an ORCID-gated professional platform. N23 database right and N24 governing law appear as ToS clauses; both need counsel before they become product. The one thing needing your decision: N22. The CC0-versus-CC BY default for external contributions is drawn on I7 with both options argued neutrally and neither pre-selected — the interface works either way, only the default state changes.
BATCH H · DOMAINS E, K AND L · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
DESIGNED · 44 of 63
Home feed with seven card variants, per-item ranking explanation with suppress controls, chronological and cross-field tabs, federated search across six types with reproducibility facets, command palette, saved search, the 600px digest, related-work and co-authorship graphs, trending by reuse, impact notifications at institution level, milestones, streaks and leaderboards (both off by default), frequency caps, share card, embed widget, Year in Review, the image feed, lab stories, video demos, and the whole AI set including per-claim sourcing, method extraction, disclosure, provenance labelling, auto-tagging and the training opt-out.
PARTIAL · 7 · AND WHY
E09 search ranking is explained but has no tuning UI. E15 topic-evolution over time is implied by the graph, not drawn. E21 feed density and object-type weighting is shown as a readout, not yet a control. K19 figure integrity screening is stated as a rule on upload; its result screen reuses F2's. L07 confidence is defined and displayed, but the calibration screen is not built. L14 model and version disclosure appears in the AI panel header without its own page.
THE EIGHT K MECHANICS · ALL NOW BUILT
I first reported K04, K06, K07, K10, K11, K12, K20, K22 as refusals; the founders' call was to keep all eight and implement them properly, on the argument that engagement aimed at replication and reuse improves the field rather than just retention. Agreed — and every one has a version whose incentive points at a verifiable act rather than at presence or volume. H8 builds all eight in their host screens: replication challenges on the method card with either outcome credited identically, data challenges scored on four axes where the raw-accuracy leader ranks seventh, endorsements weighted by endorser expertise with a zero-weight rule for reciprocal pairs, invites credited on what the invitee contributes rather than on sends, reusability prompts on datasets and projects, user-set batching, commitments to a result rather than a date, and the quarterly review published in the governance console. H7 is retained as the reference for what the naive version of each looks like. Separately, E16 and L03, L08, L09, L16 stay spec-only: each crosses from retrieval into authority.
BATCH G · DOMAINS C AND D · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
DESIGNED · 27 of 40
The whole graph and community layer: network home, the dual follow/connect model with every grant stated, non-person follows, explained suggestions, Fellow-Finder, expert finder, lab and institution pages, the four community tiers, moderator elections, the early-career space with professional escalation, the collaboration board, mentorship, office hours, events, backchannel, poster DOIs, the DM reputation gate in both states, quarantine, project channels, the technical composer, block/mute/report and notification controls.
PARTIAL · 7 · AND WHY
C10 consortium pages reuse the lab-page skeleton, but multi-site governance is undrawn. C16 role permissions appear as outcomes, not as an editor. C20 sub-communities inherit a tier; their own home is not drawn. C22 journal club is described as an event variant rather than built. D04 mentions route and create tasks; the routing-rules screen is not drawn. D09 the time-zone warning is in the composer without its scheduler. D10 broadcast exists as @project with a required reason, not as its own surface.
NOT COVERED · 6 · WITH REASONS
D06 video and voice calls and D07 voice notes — deliberately not designed. Both are commodity infrastructure every lab already has, and building a second-rate Zoom inside a research platform spends the roadmap on the one thing no user asked us for. Integrate, do not rebuild. D08 message translation and D12 retention and export are spec-only: retention is an institutional policy question belonging with the governance console, and translation carries the same misrepresentation risk already flagged for F25 and J26. C18 alumni networks and C25 organiser analytics are spec-only — the mechanisms exist (eligibility gating, community metrics); the screens do not.
BATCH F · DOMAIN J · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
DESIGNED · 26 of 30
Draft workspace, collaborative editor, citations with Zotero sync, internal review, peer challenge, the rights check in all three outcomes, paper sharing, preprint posting, version-of-record linkage, open review, reviewer invitation, post-publication comment, retraction alert, all three integrity checks, the reporting checklist, CRediT, declarations, plain-language summary, graphical abstract, submission tracker and the response workspace.
PARTIAL · 1 · AND WHY
J09 journal formatting templates — the editor has a rich-text / LaTeX switch and exports, but per-journal style packs are a content-supply problem more than a design one. Which twenty journals matter to your pilot labs is a question for you, not for us.
NOT COVERED · 3 · WITH REASONS
J26 multilingual abstract generation — spec only, and deliberately: it shares the safety question flagged for F25, since a mistranslated abstract misrepresents a result under the authors' names. J27 cover letter builder — spec only; it is the one artifact where a generated draft is worse than a blank page, because editors read hundreds. J30 registered reports — not yet. It is a genuine workflow, not a screen: a stage-1 protocol submission, in-principle acceptance, then a stage-2 results submission bound to the frozen protocol. It needs its own batch, and it should reuse the pre-registration freeze from D2 rather than duplicate it.
BATCH E · DOMAINS H AND I · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
DESIGNED · 34 of 45
The whole deposit flow and its confirmation, dataset detail with profile and codebook, version diff, five domain viewers, the visualisation builder, controlled access from both sides, storage and cost, external deposit, archival export — and on the code side the repository browser, commits, pull requests with inline review, notebook diffing, reproducible launch, the earned badge with its run record, the compute queue, secrets blocking and software citation.
PARTIAL · 8 · AND WHY
H12 residency stated, not configurable. H20 format validation shown, rule authoring not. H25 replication and a dated restore shown, the recovery runbook is not a screen. I06 CI results shown, no pipeline editor. I14 scan results shown, no policy screen. I20 fork and star counts appear, no fork-network view.
NOT COVERED · 5 · WITH REASONS
H15 instrument auto-ingest and H22 retention/legal hold are spec-only — both are institution-integration work whose UI is mostly someone else's system. I10 workflow languages appear as a launch target but CWL/Nextflow authoring is spec-only. I16 internal package registry and I19 snippet library are not yet: both are real but neither earns a screen ahead of the core loop, and a snippet library in particular competes with method cards for the same intent — worth deciding whether it should exist at all.
BATCH D · DOMAIN G · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
DESIGNED · 26 of 30
Projects list and overview, empty state, creation with discipline templates, ELN entry and day view, signing and countersign, audit trail, issue tracker, kanban and roadmap, task detail, inventory, freezer map, QR sample record, equipment booking, grant, DMP, ethics, pre-registration, hypothesis register, SOPs, risk assessment, onboarding, handover pack, PI portfolio, meeting notes, offline field mode.
PARTIAL · 2 · AND WHY
G03 private sharing circles — visibility and per-project membership are designed, but named sub-circles inside a lab need their own model and would fragment the five-value visibility chip. G30 chain of custody — every sample shows its parent, thaws and the entries that consumed it, which is a custody trail; a signed, transfer-by-transfer custody chain for regulated material is not drawn.
NOT COVERED · 2 · WITH REASONS
G15 consumables ordering and budget burn — spec only. It needs the institution's finance system, and inventing a procurement UI that no purchasing office will accept is worse than leaving the seam visible. G28 effort and time tracking per work package — deliberately not designed. Per-person time tracking contradicts the PI portfolio's stated refusal to quantify people; a researcher who believes hours are being logged stops recording honest negative results, which costs more than the reporting convenience gains. Needs a founder decision before it is built.
BATCH C · DOMAIN F · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
DESIGNED · 20 of 25
The whole core loop: composer, live retrieval, quality assistant, answered / unanswered / closed detail, promotion, method card with fork, editor and diff, negative-result post and detail, failure taxonomy, instrument hub, validation reports, tag browser, annotation layer, collections, review queue.
PARTIAL · 3 · AND WHY
F06 community wiki answers — tag wikis are designed, but a wiki-mode answer needs its own ownership and editing model that belongs with the review queue's rules. F21 bookmarks — folders designed, private notes per bookmark not drawn. F22 highlight-to-share — highlighting works, the share-snippet artifact does not exist yet.
NOT COVERED · 2 · WITH REASONS
F17 method comparison tables — spec only. A version diff compares one card to itself; comparing different methods needs a shared outcome schema we have not designed, and faking it would invite invalid comparisons. F25 post in your own language — not yet. Machine translation of a protocol is a safety question, not a convenience one; it belongs with S-domain accessibility work, not here.
BATCH B · WHAT WE COULD NOT COVER, AND WHY
NOT YET · 6 of 58
A15 vanity URL, A16 conference card / QR, A20 pseudonymous mode, A24 inbound e-mail alias, B08 written recommendations, R10 help centre. Each needs a surface that does not exist yet — A20 in particular is a whole posting flow, not a profile field, and belongs with Q&A.
SPEC CARD ONLY · 8
A04 passkeys (2FA is asserted by the IdP, so there is no SciCollab UI to draw), A09 ROR identifiers, B12 attention indicator, B16 reputation decay, B22 milestone notifications, R05 assisted migration, R09 rollout kit — all written as behaviour on the screen that would host them.
TWO CONFLICTS FOR YOU TO SETTLE
B20 field-normalised percentile contradicts B03 — a percentile is a single score wearing a disguise. Left as spec only, deliberately refused, pending your call. B05 badge tiers were specified as bronze / silver / gold; the badges are built as untiered verifiable acts instead, because a tier implies a ranking we said we would not compute.
